D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly explains register retention/removal. New Tables 7–8 distinguish five post-training configurations, document configuration-specific GPU hours and stopping information, and map reported experiments to their configurations. This substantially improves implementation traceability beyond v2's shared settings. Code and data access information is unchanged.

E1.justification: The training datasets, evaluation domains, and tasks are retained. Cityscapes, Vaihingen, NYUd depth estimation, COCO detection, and vision-language backbone evaluations already appear in v2. Additional backbone and register configurations do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond relabeling existing results as DINOv2XR, v3 adds original DINOv2 and intact-register DINOv2R comparisons in clustering, in-context retrieval, detection, and transfer evaluations (Tables 10–12 and 15). TimeT is removed from the Cityscapes comparison. These changes substantially expand comparisons against the source backbones.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 revises the stated DINOv2 global crop resolution from 224×224 to 518×518, retaining 224×224 for ablations. Table 7a qualifies the previous 25-epoch description with stopping around epoch 7. The Cityscapes evaluation switches retained backbones from ViT-S to ViT-B. These are substantial reported setting changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

The existing patch-selection, teacher, sorting, ROI-Align, training-duration, computational-control, and qualitative failure-case analyses are otherwise retained.

These are revised or additional results under clarified configurations, not established same-setting improvements. Table 5 changes only numerical precision.

M1.justification: Section 3 changes the defining training objective from CE(Qt, Qs) + CE(Qs, Qt) to CE(Qt, Qs) alone, substantively revising the specified learning objective. Feature alignment, reference sampling, differentiable sorting, and the EMA teacher remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change or a correction to the written objective.

P1.justification: V3 makes targeted revisions to the loss explanation, performance summaries, backbone terminology, and cross-references, and adds configuration explanations. The main narrative, section order, and Appendix A–D organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds configuration Tables 7–8 and expands several appendix result tables. Figure 2 switches from small-model to base-model results, displays Hummingbird instead of TimeT, and changes legends and axis ranges. Figures 1 and 3–7 retain their visual content, with appendix figures and tables relocated through reflow. The overall visual format is retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to Hummingbird, CrIBo, dense self-supervised learning, and unsupervised segmentation remain unchanged. Reference-list differences are citation-page updates caused by pagination.

T1.justification: The formal definition of the final NeCo loss in Section 3 drops the reverse cross-entropy term. The distance definitions, relaxed-swap mathematics, and sorting-matrix construction in Equations 1–7 remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

improvement.justification: V3 improves auditability by identifying register-removed checkpoints, adding intact-register comparisons, and mapping experiments to explicit configurations. It also narrows headline performance margins. These gains are limited by unresolved inconsistencies: Table 1 still labels XR baseline values as DINOv2R despite Table 10 distinguishing them, and the main 25-epoch training description is not reconciled with Table 7's early stopping. The revision therefore supports a limited overall quality improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeCo study and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. Content can be matched across table renumbering, relocation, and revised DINOv2 variant names.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional comparisons involving original DINOv2, intact-register DINOv2R, and register-removed DINOv2XR.

before.justification: V2 reports original NeCo results for segmentation, in-context retrieval, multiview correspondence, detection, depth estimation, and ablations in the main text and Appendix B.

title: Near, far: Patch-ordering enhances vision foundation models' scene understanding

C1.justification: V2 strengthens the efficiency claim to one-shot refinement, including outperforming NeFeS with DFNet on 7Scenes, where v1 said two rounds were needed. The central contributions and claims about improving APR/SCR localization and achieving leading indoor accuracy otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 adds substantive arguments about feature-map information loss, one matching operation versus HLoc's multiple retrieved images, and greater query overlap from rendered views. V2 removes v1's discussion of iteration-dependent convergence and the relationship between initial-pose accuracy and refined accuracy. The limitation that GSLocrel degrades accurate ACE estimates remains.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix A.1 newly identifies prebuilt COLMAP/HLoc model sources and describes using dataset depth maps and rendered depth to improve the 7Scenes sparse point cloud. V1 specified COLMAP sparse initialization without these details. This improves disclosure but does not establish when the procedure was introduced. Hardware, training iterations, resizing, ACT settings, and the project-page address remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three localization benchmarks and indoor/outdoor scene coverage. Added masking and retrieval illustrations concern existing scenes. Removing dSLAM-based localization results changes ground-truth evaluation coverage, rather than the represented environments or localization task.

E2.justification: V2 adds pNeRFLoc to the 7Scenes comparison, PMNet to Cambridge, and a qualitative NetVLAD retrieval comparison. It drops supplementary sequential-APR comparisons involving VLocNet, MapNet+PGO, AtLoc+, and TransAPR variants. MCLoc was already compared in v1's appendix; its main-text appearance is principally relocation.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 2cm/2° recall threshold for 7Scenes and mask/ACT controls for qualitative rendering comparisons. Main DFNet results emphasize one-step refinement, already tested in v1 Table 13, while two-step controls and dSLAM localization evaluation disappear. The stated image resolutions, training budget, and default SfM ground truth remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 removes the iteration/convergence study in v1 Section 8 and Table 13 and the localization sensitivity comparison between dSLAM and SfM poses in Table 11. It adds mask/ACT rendering comparisons and a retrieval-versus-rendering overlap case study in Figures 9–10. Matcher and ACT ablations and the ground-truth rendering-quality comparison remain.

E5.justification: Both runtime sections state that measurements are averaged over 1,000 runs. Neither version reports localization seed variation, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests; v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Reported one-shot DFNet+GSLoc error on 7Scenes changes from 4.0cm/1.0° in v1 Table 13 to 1.1cm/0.34° in v2 Table 1. Marepo+GSLoc's 12Scenes recall changes from 70.3% to 90.9%, and NeRFMatch's 7Scenes recall from 75.4% to 78.4%. Matcher-ablation scores also change, stricter recall results are added, and supplementary result entries disappear. These are revised reports, without an established explanation for all underlying experimental differences.

M1.justification: V2 removes the optional iterative feedback procedure described in v1 Section 3.2 and drawn in its pipeline figures, retaining single-pass refinement. The underlying 3DGS, ACT, MASt3R, PnP/RANSAC, and GSLocrel components remain unchanged; newly disclosed reconstruction details do not establish a new core algorithm.

P1.justification: V2 edits the introduction, shortens the conclusion, swaps the Cambridge and 12Scenes discussion order, and reorganizes the supplement into Appendix A.1–A.4. One-shot terminology replaces iteration-specific language. Most main-text organization and method exposition remain closely matched.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two columns to one, adds a front-page teaser, redraws pipeline diagrams without iterative feedback, merges the GSLocrel comparison tables, and transposes runtime and matcher tables. It adds segmentation and retrieval figures and reorganizes qualitative examples; Figure 11 partly redisplays examples already present in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds literature on PMNet, pNeRFLoc, parallel NeRF inversion, image-retrieval benchmarking, LaMAR, and Air-HLoc. References supporting removed sequential-APR comparisons disappear, as does the DUSt3R reference despite retaining that matcher. Appendix A.3 expands positioning against retrieval and rendering-based approaches, while the main related-work framework remains similar.

T1.justification: The ACT transformation, Gaussian depth-rendering expression, and relative-pose composition equations remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. The removed 'Accuracy Bound' section reports empirical iteration behavior rather than a mathematical bound.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful reconstruction details, stricter 7Scenes evaluation, and visual evidence about masking. However, its appendix removes quantitative evidence about convergence and sensitivity to ground-truth poses. Large revised indoor scores, including Marepo's 12Scenes recall changing from 70.3% to 90.9%, lack a clear accompanying explanation of procedural changes. The gains in documentation and evaluation detail coexist with losses in diagnostic evidence, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GSLoc research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved from v1's supplement into v2's main text.

after.justification: V2 retains original localization experiments, runtime measurements, and ablations, with revised numerical results and additional qualitative segmentation and retrieval comparisons.

before.justification: V1 reports original localization experiments on 7Scenes, 12Scenes, and Cambridge Landmarks, runtime measurements, matcher and ACT ablations, and supplementary ground-truth and iteration studies.

title: GS-CPR: Efficient Camera Pose Refinement via 3D Gaussian Splatting

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: one-shot refinement using 3DGS and MASt3R, exposure adaptation, improved APR/SCR localization, greater accuracy and speed than NeRF-based optimization, and state-of-the-art results on two indoor datasets. Renaming and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5 newly identifies failures caused by inaccurate initial poses and insufficient image overlap, and acknowledges difficulties reconstructing large scenes. Appendix A.3 expands the explanation of metric depth, global scale, and synthesized versus retrieved reference views. Appendix A.6 distinguishes strong indoor GLACE improvements from mainly rotational gains on Cambridge. These materially expand applicability boundaries and mechanism interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 specifies HLoc's SuperPoint/SuperGlue configuration and attributes the revised Cambridge GLACE results to official models. It also changes the runtime GPU designation from GTX 4090 to RTX 4090 and revises the COLMAP-model provenance wording in Appendix A.1. These are limited documentation changes; the principal hyperparameters and project-page access information remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The three datasets remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 adds a controlled input scenario using synthetically perturbed ground-truth initial poses on ShopFacade, extending evaluation beyond pose-estimator outputs. The additional GLACE evaluations reuse existing dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds HLoc with SuperPoint and SuperGlue to the Cambridge comparison; its existing 7Scenes participation is merely relabeled more explicitly. Figure 10 adds ACE-pose-based reference-image retrieval alongside NetVLAD.

E3.justification: Table 4 extends 12Scenes evaluation to median translation/rotation errors and 5cm/5-degree recall. New experiments independently perturb rotation and translation on ShopFacade and evaluate GLACE as an initializer. Figure 10 switches the rendered-view initializer from DFNet to ACE. These are extensions within retained benchmarks, without a documented change to the main training budget.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 introduces a systematic initial-pose sensitivity study over rotational and translational perturbations, supported by Tables 10–11 and a failure example in Figure 12. Figure 10 expands a single retrieval illustration into three scene comparisons with correspondence counts. These substantially extend robustness and diagnostic evidence beyond the retained ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions average runtime measurements over 1,000 runs. v3 introduces no new seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the added perturbation results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds GLACE refinement results across all three benchmarks, perturbation outcomes, matching counts, and Cambridge HLoc results. Table 4 adds aggregate 12Scenes metrics but removes the per-scene 2cm/2-degree scores, retaining their averages. Table 3 revises GLACE's Cambridge scores, changing its reported average from 13cm/0.32 degrees to 14cm/0.32 degrees. Table 6 changes DFNet plus the relative variant from 0.07 to 0.08 seconds and ACE plus refinement from 0.18 to 0.19 seconds. Most retained headline accuracy results are unchanged.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the relative variant's stated translation update from t_hat + s R_rel t_rel to R_rel t_hat + s t_rel. The main 3DGS, ACT, MASt3R, and PnP pipeline remains unchanged. This establishes a revision to the published inference rule, without establishing an implementation change or rerun.

P1.justification: GSLoc becomes GS-CPR throughout, publication and author formatting change, and citations receive consistent parentheses. Appendix A.3 gains explanatory prose and A.5–A.6 are added, but the existing narrative and section sequence are largely retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 10 is rebuilt as a full-page, three-scene correspondence comparison; Figure 12 and Tables 10–13 are added. Table 4 changes from a scene-by-scene layout to an aggregate multi-metric comparison, and Figure 3 explicitly marks the scale path and highlights the variant's differing component. These substantially expand and restructure the evidence displays, alongside relocation of retained material.

R1.justification: v3 adds DeTone et al. (2018) for SuperPoint and Jiao et al. (2024), LiteVLoc, as a depth-camera-based approach contrasted with its metric-depth rendering. The main related-work taxonomy and positioning remain intact; the Air-HLoc reference update is bibliographic.

T1.justification: Equation 3 revises the mathematical pose composition by changing which translation is multiplied by the relative rotation. This is an algebraically substantive correction, rather than equivalent notation. Equations 1–2 are retained, and neither version contains a separate theorem or proof development.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the paper through the corrected pose-composition equation, explicit failure analysis, controlled perturbation tests, and broader comparator and initializer evidence. The gain is limited by removing per-scene 12Scenes results and retaining Appendix A.3's broad HLoc-superiority statement despite the newly added Cambridge comparison favoring HLoc. Overall, the additions improve support and clarify applicability while leaving the core findings largely unchanged.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same camera-pose refinement work, renamed from GSLoc to GS-CPR. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds pose-perturbation tests, GLACE refinement results, and expanded matching comparisons in its appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original localization experiments on 7Scenes, 12Scenes, and Cambridge Landmarks, plus runtime, matcher, exposure-adaptation, and rendering analyses.

title: GS-CPR: Efficient Camera Pose Refinement via 3D Gaussian Splatting

C1.justification: v2 foregrounds provable convergence in the abstract and introduction as an explicit contribution, although the supporting proofs already existed in v1. The principal conflict-free optimization, momentum acceleration and PINN/MTL performance claims remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v1 mainly discusses M-ConFIG's degradation with many losses and its memory requirements. v2 adds substantive applicability boundaries: loss balancing alone cannot resolve anisotropic scaling or chaotic dynamics. It explains the KS failure through multiscale derivative-resolution difficulties and discusses architectural changes and causality as complementary directions.

D1.justification: Appendices A.11-A.12 document the new PDEs' equations, domains, boundary/initial conditions and training sample allocations and budgets. Existing architecture, optimizer settings, sampling procedure, hardware and code-access information are retained; training details move from A.11 to A.12.

E1.justification: Appendix A.11 adds five-dimensional Poisson, anisotropic multiscale heat transfer and chaotic KS problems. These substantially broaden the tested dimensionality and physical regimes beyond v1's four PDE cases. Existing PDE and CelebA coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 1-19 retain the same methods. The new PDE tests reuse the existing PINN baseline pool. Newly cited Jacobian-descent and dual-cone methods are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.13 adds an evaluation design varying cosine-decay schedules, constant learning rates, collocation sample counts and boundary/interior sampling ratios. Table 23 also specifies training allocations for the three new PDE cases. The stated protocols for retained experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic learning-rate and sampling sensitivity analyses in Tables 24-27 and Figure 26. Appendix A.11 also investigates unresolved anisotropic structure and explicitly examines chaotic dynamics as a failure case. Existing direction-weight and momentum analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three runs with different random seeds and report means and standard deviations. Added results follow this existing practice; no increased run count, new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1-19 are retained, while Tables 20-22 and 24-27 add substantial benchmark and sensitivity results. For example, PNd MSE is (0.415 +/- 0.052) x 10^-6 for M-ConFIG versus (1.916 +/- 0.284) x 10^-6 for Adam. Added findings also include incomplete HeatMS reconstruction and failure to capture chaotic KS dynamics.

M1.justification: The normalized-gradient pseudoinverse, equal projection weighting, adaptive magnitude and alternating momentum updates remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1, 3 and 4. The additional experiments do not introduce a new method component.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing exposition remain intact. Changes include local abstract and runtime-explanation edits, additional subsection headings, appendix organization, and conversion to author-year citations and conference headings.

P2.justification: v2 adds solution-comparison and sampling-sensitivity displays in Figures 23-26, seven benchmark/ablation result tables, and an expanded settings table. It also adopts ICLR headers and typography, changes table rules, and resizes or relocates retained figures and tables.

R1.justification: v2 adds Quinton and Rey's Jacobian descent, Hwang and Lim's concurrent dual-cone gradient descent, and Hao et al.'s PINNacle benchmark. These modestly extend positioning and benchmark attribution; the existing related-work discussion is largely retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds a short storage-complexity argument giving O(nm) costs for per-loss gradients and momentum. The convergence theorems, assumptions and proofs, and the existence and equivalence arguments in A.1-A.4, are retained rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: The challenging PDE tests and hyperparameter ablations provide useful evidence about robustness and applicability beyond v1. Explicit HeatMS and KS failure discussions also clarify limitations. However, the new Section 4.1 claim of consistent superiority on challenging PDEs overstates Table 22, where neither variant leads and M-ConFIG performs worse than Adam. The added evidence improves the paper, but its summary claims are not fully aligned with that evidence.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConFIG and M-ConFIG work. Their main texts, appendices, equations, figures and tables are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added material.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original results for three challenging PDE problems and learning-rate and sampling ablations.

before.justification: v1 reports original PINN experiments on four PDE cases and CelebA multi-task experiments, including numerical results, runtime comparisons and ablations.

title: ConFIG: Towards Conflict-free Training of Physics Informed Neural Networks

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about conflict-free updates, balanced projections, adaptive magnitudes, momentum acceleration, and performance on PINNs and multi-task learning.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and limitations concerning momentum-update frequency, memory, and difficult PDEs remain unchanged. The Section 4.2 wording correction restates the updates-per-iteration interpretation already explicitly explained in v2.

D1.justification: Implementation guidance, hyperparameters, sampling instructions, hardware, training times, and sample counts in Appendices A.5 and A.12 and Table 23 are unchanged. Code-access statements and external link targets also remain identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four main PINN cases, the PNd, HeatMS, and KS problems in Appendix A.11, and the same CelebA task configurations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. The PINN comparisons retain their existing baselines, and CelebA Tables 14–15 retain the same ten comparison methods.

E3.justification: Metrics, training budgets, sampling, model configurations, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Section 4.2 replaces 'iterations' with 'gradient update', but the explicit updates-per-iteration setting and the experiments in Tables 18–19 already appear in v2.

E4.justification: Direction-weight tests, momentum-strategy comparisons, task/update-count analyses, challenging-PDE failure analyses, and learning-rate/sample-count ablations are retained unchanged in Figure 8, Figure 12, and Appendices A.5, A.11, and A.13.

E5.justification: Both versions specify averaging three training runs initialized with different random seeds and retain the same standard-deviation reporting in the appendix tables. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 15 retains best CelebA F1 scores of 0.694 ± 0.005 for M-ConFIG 30 and 0.686 ± 0.006 for ConFIG; the edited captions do not alter table entries.

M1.justification: The ConFIG gradient construction, magnitude adjustment, and M-ConFIG momentum procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and the appendix algorithms. The wording edit in Section 4.2 does not introduce a procedural change.

P1.justification: Limited edits standardize ConFIG capitalization, including the Appendix A.5 heading and several captions, and replace 'number of iterations' with 'number of gradient update' in Section 4.2. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; section order and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 12 and Tables 16–19 receive caption edits and local line rewrapping. Table 18 introduces the stray text 'METof'; plots, table structures, axes, legends, and figure/table placement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the positioning against PCGrad and IMTL-G in Section 3.2, and the bibliography are unchanged. No cited work or substantive research positioning is added or removed.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions, convergence theorems and proofs, comparator derivations, and solution-existence and equivalence arguments in Appendices A.1–A.4 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves naming consistency and clarifies a sentence whose updates-per-iteration meaning was already explicit in v2. These small editorial gains accompany a new 'METof' typo in Table 18. With methods, evidence, theory, and reproducibility information unchanged, the edits do not materially alter overall paper quality.

A1.justification: Both 36-page PDFs describe the same ConFIG research and include Appendices A.1–A.13. Text comparison, full-page rendering comparison, and inspection of the differing pages support reliable comparison without material gaps.

after.justification: v3 retains the original PINN and CelebA experiments, including numerical results and supplementary analyses in Appendices A.5–A.13.

before.justification: v2 reports original PINN training and CelebA multi-task experiments in Section 4, with numerical results, runtime measurements, additional PDE experiments, and ablations in the appendices.

title: ConFIG: Towards Conflict-free Training of Physics Informed Neural Networks

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and discussion retain the claims about abstraction, discriminative world modelling, sample efficiency, transfer, planning and learning abstraction components. Additional comparisons support these claims without materially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1.3 adds explanations of attention-mediated object interactions and the restrictions of NCS-style dynamics; B.1.4 develops possible robotics applications. The existing limitations concerning labelled object mappings and failures of single-item planning are retained.

D1.justification: v2 expands the attention architecture description and documents the learned encoder's observation/action inputs, convolutional encoder, output heads, loss, batch size and learning rate. Appendix G.3 adds MuZero's implementation source, search ranges and selected settings. These address substantial implementation gaps in v1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same three 2D Crafting tasks, five MiniHack skill environments, sandbox transfer and compositional scenario. New experiments reuse this coverage. The robotics examples in v2 Table 1 are proposed applications, not evaluated domains.

E2.justification: v2 adds MuZero to the five MiniHack comparisons in Figure 4b and NCS-style k-means/greedy planning plus a k-means/Dijkstra variant in Appendix F.1.3 and Figure 23. Existing comparators remain. DAC-MDP and DLP-EIT appear in the conceptual comparison table without corresponding benchmark results.

E3.justification: Additional protocols vary encoder training fractions from 1% to 90%, fixed optimization budgets from 100 to 2500 steps, Dreamer training ratios and MuZero self-play delays. These substantially expand controlled evaluation; the original benchmark metrics and default MEAD, Dreamer and PPO settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds encoder-data sensitivity and downstream planning analysis (Figure 25), an additional fixed-budget optimization analysis (Figure 30), and Dreamer/MuZero training-setting analyses (Figures 35–36). Figure 23 also compares greedy versus Dijkstra planning with the NCS-style model. Earlier ablations remain.

E5.justification: v1 states a minimum of three independent seeds. v2 Table 6 specifies counts by main experiment and method, including four/five MEAD seeds for Crafting/MiniHack. This is additional disclosure, not evidence of increased runs. Existing confidence-interval and stated exception conventions are retained.

E6.justification: New MuZero, NCS and sensitivity results materially expand the evidence. v2 Figure 23 shows the k-means/Dijkstra variant failing four-step Crafting but learning in Freeze-Wand; Figure 25 shows poor planning with very small encoder datasets. Retained main mean curves are unchanged, although some confidence bands differ slightly.

M1.justification: The discriminative transition model, count-based exploration, MCTS, Dijkstra planning and training algorithm are retained. Expanded attention-network and learned-map descriptions document existing components; the PDFs do not establish a changed MEAD procedure.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main-section/Appendix A–G organization are retained. v2 makes local wording corrections, expands explanations, introduces targeted appendix subsections and consolidates the semantic-embedding headings, without extensively rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds five experimental figures and four tables, expands Figure 14 into three environment panels, and revises Figure 4's comparator display and Figure 11's labels. It also changes title/heading styling and introduces running headers throughout. Most earlier graphics remain, often relocated or renumbered.

R1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B.1.3 substantially expand positioning against object-centric research, including NCS, DLP-based methods and CEE-US. Table 5 compares representation, function approximation and planning choices. Additional MuZero and robotics references extend this substantive comparison beyond bibliographic restyling.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.1.3 supplies mathematical correspondences between Ab-MDP and OO-MDP, NCS and DLP representations, including a comparison of transition-dependency assumptions. The existing Ab-MDP definitions, Remark B.3 and single-/multi-item counterexample analysis remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by adding online-planning and object-structured comparators missing from v1, including a control separating model choice from planning choice. Encoder-data and training-budget analyses better expose performance dependencies, while fuller implementation and seed reporting improve reproducibility. These gains address important comparison and documentation gaps; the dependence on supplied or supervised abstractions remains.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ab-MDP/MEAD work. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds baseline comparisons and sensitivity analyses, including Figures 23, 25, 30, 35 and 36.

before.justification: v1 reports original 2D Crafting and MiniHack experiments, transfer results, learned-component evaluations and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix F.

title: Efficient Exploration and Discriminative World Model Learning with an Object-Centric Abstraction

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions and claims about sample efficiency, transfer, interpretable world models, and learning abstraction components. The expanded discussion does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly explains that discrete attributes cannot precisely capture continuous quantities such as position and velocity, while low-level policies can still use continuous features and actions. The existing limitation concerning supervised object mappings is retained.

D1.justification: Implementation details, architecture, data processing, hardware disclosures, hyperparameters, and resource links are unchanged (Appendices A, C, D, and G; Tables 7–10). Repositioned technical material supplies no additional reproducibility information.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three 2D Crafting environments, five MiniHack skill games, sandbox transfer, and Levitate-then-Freeze compositional task. The robotics examples in Table 1 remain illustrative constructions, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain PPO, Dreamer-v3, MuZero, the nonparametric attribute planner, and NCS/k-means comparisons (Figures 4, 17–23). Factored MDPs are newly discussed as related work, without an added evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, budgets, preprocessing, model configurations, and experimental procedures are unchanged. Both retain 200k-frame transfer pretraining, the 100k-transition encoder dataset, and the settings in Appendices D, F, and G.

E4.justification: The model, exploration, embedding, optimization, and learned-component analyses are retained. The single-item failure example and replanning discussion in Appendix B.2.2, and the representation and world-graph analyses in Appendix F, already appear in v2.

E5.justification: Table 6 reports identical seed counts. Both versions retain 95% confidence intervals for main results, standard deviation for encoder accuracy in Figure 6, and standard error for Figure 7 as specified in Appendix F.3.1.

E6.justification: The corresponding performance curves, ablation results, encoder accuracies, and world-model transition probabilities are unchanged. Main and appendix figures retain the same findings; their relocation introduces no new or revised results.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix C retain the same abstraction, discriminative success model, count-based MCTS exploration, and Dijkstra goal planning. The added factored-MDP discussion does not modify the method.

P1.justification: Localized expansions affect related work, Appendix B.1.3, and the discussion, with an added closing paragraph. Affiliations, acknowledgments, and the publication header are updated. The section hierarchy and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables are repositioned as text reflows, while their designs, axes, legends, and captions remain unchanged. For example, Table 7 now appears alongside Section G.1, and Table 10 moves after Figures 35–36.

R1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B.1.3 add factored-MDP positioning and four references: Boutilier et al. (1995, 1999), Guestrin et al. (2003), and Degris and Sigaud (2013). The addition distinguishes action-dependent transition factorizations from Ab-MDP's item-change actions and learned dynamics.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1.3 adds a formal description of factored states and their Dynamic Bayesian Network transition factorization (v3 Equation 6), explaining its relationship to Ab-MDP. improvement.justification: v4 addresses important validation gaps in v3 through component ablations, specialized detector comparisons and external-generator tests that expose generalization failures (Tables 7–9). A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SONICS dataset and SpecTTTra research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and additionally reports token ablations, external-generator evaluations, specialized detector comparisons and dataset-quality checks.

before.justification: v3 reports original detection experiments, a human evaluation and efficiency measurements in Section 4 and Tables 2, 4–6, alongside dataset analyses in the appendices.

title: SONICS: Synthetic Or Not - Identifying Counterfeit Songs

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates and averages across tasks. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the inconsistent multiplier in the calibration-cost calculation and clarifies block-versus-layer terminology, improving internal consistency and readability. The experiments, claims, and appendix proofs remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized edits to baseline descriptions and algorithm comments, adds the architecture overview in A.3 and appendix subsections A.4–A.5, and introduces acknowledgments and the ICLR publication header. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds the authors' MaskLLM training and evaluation in A.4 and LoRA fine-tuning experiments in A.5. The separately cited MaskLLM speedup is distinguished from these original experiments.

before.justification: v2 reports original activation analyses, perplexity and downstream-task evaluations, and kernel and decoding-speed measurements. Appendix A.2 supplies detailed task results.

title: Instruct-SkillMix: A Powerful Pipeline for LLM Instruction Tuning

BLOOMZ's removed five-epoch statement prevents confirming identical training conditions. Retained main-table rows and the 201-language results table otherwise match.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 adds rank-16 LoRA fine-tuning of PaLM2 S, changing which parameters are updated. The core multilingual postediting and sequence-distillation procedures remain unchanged; using the same teacher and student model was already permitted in v1.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose revisions, expands Section 4.3, reorders part of related work, adds acknowledgments and a BLEU appendix subsection, and corrects cross-references. The introduction, method narrative, and most existing appendix explanations remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains model and ablation rows, while Figure 2 adds PaLM2 S and LoRA with adjusted axes and legends. New BLEU Tables 6–7 and Figure 4 reuse existing comparison formats. Table 3 and appendix material are reflowed or renumbered; the method diagram and attention examples are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for BLEU, LoRA, adaptation-related forgetting, and differences between human and model translations, including Papineni, Hu, Biderman, Sizov, Zhang, and Kocmi. Its positioning relative to in-context learning, multilingual reasoning, and low-resource translation remains largely unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theorems, proofs, or derivations. V2's clearer explanation of win percentages restates the existing metric rather than changing its mathematical definition.

improvement.justification: The BLEU checks and targeted ablations strengthen empirical support and clarify tuning and auxiliary-context tradeoffs; the cost discussion is more concrete. These gains are tempered by removed reproducibility details and an unrevised ablation interpretation: new Gemma 7B results show mufu5tr below postediting alone, 42.9 versus 46.3 FLORES chrF, contrary to Section 4.3's general statement. Overall, the additions provide a limited net quality improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mufu research. Their text, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content across relocation and renumbering.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and reports additional PaLM2 S, LoRA, auxiliary-language ablation, and BLEU results.

before.justification: V1 reports original FLORES-200 and NTREX translation experiments, including fine-tuning, distillation, ablations, and attention analyses.

title: Mufu:  Multilingual Fused Learning for Low-Resource Translation with LLM

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain identical claims about data-efficient low-resource translation, multilingual reasoning, robustness, and distillation.

C2.justification: The attention-based explanations, overfitting and domain-shift interpretations, poor-auxiliary failure conditions, and inference-cost limitations remain unchanged, including the appendix discussion.

D1.justification: Prompt templates, auxiliary-language lists, learning rates, training and decoding details, and model/data access information are identical. PDF hyperlink targets also match.

E1.justification: Both retain FLORES-200 evaluation over 201 English-to-target directions and NTREX over 112. Pretraining and distillation data, language/script coverage, and appendix scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baseline and postediting variants, PaLM2 S teacher, NLLB 1.3B distilled, and NLLB 54B MoE comparators. Appendix comparator membership also matches.

E3.justification: Data splits, chrF/BLEU metrics, model configurations, training budgets, checkpoint selection, and decoding procedures are identical in Section 3 and Appendix A.3.

E4.justification: The auxiliary-language and postediting ablations, LoRA and distillation analyses, attention studies, domain-shift evaluation, and failure examples are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Figures 2 and 4 retain identical 95% confidence intervals across language pairs. No run-count, seed, or statistical-procedure information is added, removed, or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including the main chrF results, appendix BLEU and per-language scores, BLOOMZ results, plotted findings, and translation examples.

M1.justification: The teacher-generated auxiliary translations, student postediting and finetuning, language selection, and distillation procedures are identical.

P1.justification: v3 adds the running header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025'. Body prose, terminology, author information, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The publication header appears on every page in v3. Figures, tables, captions, axes, legends, pagination, and all content below the header render identically.

R1.justification: Section 5, citations, bibliography, and positioning relative to prior work are identical. The publication notice does not alter the research positioning.

T1.justification: Mathematical content and reasoning are identical. No definitions, formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added, removed, or revised.

improvement.justification: v3 adds only the ICLR 2025 publication header. Scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation remain identical throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.

A1.justification: Both contain the same 31-page Mufu paper, including Appendices A.1-A.8. Page-by-page text and rendering comparisons establish identical substantive content; the only visible difference is v3's publication header.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original translation experiments and results, including the main-text evaluations and appendix analyses.

before.justification: v2 reports original translation experiments on FLORES-200 and NTREX, including chrF/BLEU results, ablations, attention analyses, and appendix BLOOMZ evaluations.

title: Mufu:  Multilingual Fused Learning for Low-Resource Translation with LLM

C1.justification: Both versions claim that blockwise KV reuse with fine-tuning preserves RAG accuracy while sharply reducing first-token latency and computation. v4 foregrounds computational cost in its title and abstract, but FLOP savings were already claimed in v1's introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v4 newly interprets the position ablation as evidence that re-encoding is essential. It also argues that Prompt Cache's position dependence restricts reuse when passage rankings change. The existing passage-interference conjecture, exclusion of cache costs and discussion of broader applications remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 removes v1's project-code availability footnote, adds a DeepSpeed access link, explicitly identifies Flash-Attention for inference, and revises the training-backend description. Hardware and numerical hyperparameters are retained. Removal of the code-link disclosure does not establish that the repository itself became unavailable.

E1.justification: Both versions train on TriviaQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA and evaluate on those datasets plus Natural Questions and HotpotQA. The cached-passage efficiency scenarios are retained. Code generation and dialogue remain suggested applications rather than evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: The vanilla and block-without-fine-tuning baselines persist under revised names. v4 adds fine-tuned models without position re-encoding for both backbones. Section 3.3 also reports a Prompt Cache reimplementation matching the weak-baseline rows and a qualitative PCW comparison below those baselines, without separate PCW scores.

E3.justification: v4 introduces the control that disables position re-encoding. Its reported training setup also changes from explicit Flash-Attention V2 for SFT and SDPA for block training to a general Flash-Attention V2 description; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. Model sizes, optimization hyperparameters, answer-matching accuracy and the 200-token output limit remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's fine-tuning comparison and checkpoint analysis, v4 tests the contribution of another central method component: position re-encoding. Table 1 ablates it across both backbones and all four benchmarks, reporting mixed-average losses of 4.5 points for Llama3 and 3.5 for Mistral. This supplies previously absent component-level validation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v4's added domain averages summarize benchmark accuracy, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds complete position-ablation results and in-/out-domain averages. Mistral-block's TQA/2Wiki/NQ/HQA scores change from 70.7/69.0/50.5/58.6 to 69.9/70.5/50.8/57.9, and its aggregate changes from 62.8 to 62.3. Llama3's weak-baseline 2Wiki and NQ scores change from 42.1 and 43.2 to 48.1 and 43.3. Figure 4 adds zero-step points while retaining the subsequent trajectories. These materially expand and revise reported evidence; Table 2's latency and FLOP values remain unchanged.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.5 retain the same independent-block attention mask, passage segmentation, RoPE position adjustment, block fine-tuning and cached inference procedure. The new experiments disable an existing component; they do not introduce a new proposed method.

P1.justification: The title changes from Low-Latency RAG to Efficient RAG, and the abstract and selected introductory and experimental passages are rewritten. Experimental setup paragraphs become numbered subsections, training and evaluation descriptions are separated, and related work is inserted. Much of the method and discussion wording remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains ablation rows, domain-average columns and stronger visual emphasis. Figure 3 adds explicit document/query divisions, Figure 2 updates terminology, and Figure 4 expands its vertical range for the added zero-step points. Table 2 relabels its first prompt-length column from 0 to 50. The same four figures and two tables are retained.

R1.justification: v1 lacks a dedicated related-work discussion. v4 adds Section 4 covering RAG and inference efficiency, substantially expanding citations and positioning against FiD, PCW, Prompt Cache and RAGCache. It explicitly distinguishes architecture compatibility, context-window objectives and position-dependent cache reuse.

T1.justification: The sequence/KV definitions and three RoPE equations are retained with equivalent mathematical content. Neither version supplies additional theorems, proofs or formal assumptions.

improvement.justification: The new position ablation supplies useful evidence absent from v1: disabling re-encoding reduces accuracy on every benchmark for both models. Section 4 also improves research positioning. These gains are tempered by reporting defects: v4's abstract retains 62.8 while Table 1 reports 62.3 for Mistral, and its Llama3-vanilla in-domain average of 73.9 exceeds both constituent scores, 72.8 and 73.4. Together with removal of the project-code link, these problems limit the overall improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Block-Attention research. All nine pages of v1 and twelve pages of v4, including equations, figures, tables and references, support comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark and efficiency results and adds position-re-encoding ablations and further accuracy summaries.

before.justification: v1 reports original four-benchmark accuracy results, checkpoint evaluations, and latency/FLOP measurements in Tables 1–2 and Figure 4.

title: Block-Attention for Efficient Prefilling

C1.justification: v4's central validation concerns maintaining RAG accuracy while reducing prefilling cost. v5 broadens the claimed contribution to general and ICL capabilities, adds lossless switching between block and full attention as a central claim, and highlights game-AI applications in the abstract. The headline 32K latency/FLOPs reduction claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v5 interprets joint training as enabling both attention modes and removes v4's conjecture that passage independence might make block attention intrinsically more accurate. PromptCache's critique shifts from restrictive cache reuse to positional-encoding-related quality degradation. Discussion emphasizes real-time game agents instead of ReAct, and a new qualification explains the absence of subjective evaluations requiring OpenAI API access.

D1.justification: v5 announces public code, datasets, and model weights and supplies a project access link. It documents Tulu3 segmentation rules, the usable 23% fraction, and OpenCompass evaluation. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Conversely, v4's explicit DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage-2 and Flash-Attention V2 specifications are omitted.

E1.justification: v5 adds Tulu3 SFT training data, seven reported general/ICL benchmarks (MMLU, BBH, DROP, MATH, GSM8K, HumanEval, and IFEval), and an internal game scenario in Appendix A. The four original RAG benchmarks remain. NarrativeQA is also named, but its actual evaluation is unclear because no corresponding results are reported.

E2.justification: The reported comparison set expands to include Superposition and an original Tulu3-SFT control alongside the RAG-fine-tuned full-attention baseline. PromptCache was already evaluated in v4 through results identified as identical to its weak baselines; v5 reports it separately from block-without-fine-tuning, with distinct outcomes. The no-fine-tuning and no-position comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Sections 3.1-3.4 replace Llama3-8B/Mistral-7B with Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-SFT and replace GPT-4-generated RAG answers with Llama3.3-70B-Instruct answers. Added evaluations use zero-shot general tests, four-shot GSM8K/MATH, and three-shot BBH/DROP. Hardware is reported as eight H20s rather than eight A800s; this does not establish that the unchanged timing results were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds a full-attention fallback ablation testing whether the block-trained model retains compatibility with full attention. Figure 4 changes from comparing separately trained models to comparing two attention modes of the adapted model. Existing fine-tuning and positional ablations remain, while Appendix A adds a game-state reuse case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Benchmark averages and checkpoint curves do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The Llama3/Mistral accuracy table is replaced by Tulu3 results, and seven-task results are added. Figure 4's reported adaptation point changes from about 400 to 800 steps under different training conditions. Appendix A reports TTFT decreasing from 2,800 to 100 ms. These are new or replaced results, not same-setting improvements over v4. The original latency/FLOPs table is numerically unchanged, moving from Table 2 to Table 3.

M1.justification: v4 adapts models through block-mask fine-tuning. v5 explicitly trains every training sample under both block and full attention to preserve both operating modes, substantially changing the training procedure. It also specifies segmentation of general SFT examples by turns, messages, and delimiters. The underlying block mask, cache reuse, and RoPE operations remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes from Efficient RAG to Efficient Prefilling. The abstract, experimental narrative, baseline descriptions, and results discussion are substantially rewritten. Related work is reorganized into three subsections, and acknowledgements and a game appendix are added. Author, affiliation, conference-header, and attention terminology edits accompany this restructuring.

P2.justification: v5 adds the general/ICL Table 2 and game illustration Figure 5. Table 1 drops the three average columns and reorders datasets. Figure 4 is redrawn with revised axes, legends, and curves; Figures 2 and 4 use text-wrapped placement. The unchanged efficiency table is relocated and renumbered Table 3.

R1.justification: A new concurrent-work section credits TurboRAG's independent similar contribution and distinguishes the approach from DecoupledRAG, NSA, and MoBA. Parallel-context positioning expands through Superposition, SGLang, and CacheBlend. The earlier general discussion of linear attention, mixture-of-experts, speculative decoding, and RAGCache is removed; PCW's duplicate references are consolidated.

T1.justification: The KV-state definitions and RoPE derivation in Equations 1-3 are unchanged. Appendix A's conditional-probability notation illustrates game tasks but adds no substantive mathematical reasoning, formal assumptions, or proofs.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens practical validation by directly testing general-capability retention and switching back to full attention, concerns left untested in v4. The switching ablation, general/ICL evaluations, additional comparator, and new resource-access information improve evidential coverage and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by losing Mistral coverage, limited game-experiment documentation, and overstated accuracy claims: Section 3.5 claims RAG gaps of at most 1%, while Table 1 reports HQA scores of 72.3 versus 74.8. These weaknesses limit the conclusions but do not outweigh the substantial added validation.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Block-Attention research, despite the revised title and expanded scope. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v4 has no appendix; v5's Appendix A is available and included.

after.justification: Section 3 reports RAG, general-capability, and in-context-learning experiments. Appendix A additionally reports original latency outcomes from an internal game application.

before.justification: Section 3 reports original RAG accuracy experiments, ablations, training curves, and latency/FLOPs measurements in Tables 1-2 and Figure 4.

title: Block-Attention for Efficient Prefilling

C1.justification: The main claims about tunable Matérn reconstruction, computational efficiency and learned kernels persist. The introduction adds superiority for high-frequency texture reconstruction and explicitly claims more than fourfold faster training than NKF. The introduction and conclusion also elevate the existing reconstruction-error bound and bandwidth guidance into an explicit contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explains stationarity through centering requirements and consistency between repeated objects, qualifies v1's compact-support assertion as exponential decay and effective compactness, and recommends h = 1 as a starting point. It also interprets sharper textures as evidence against spectral bias, although its blanket texture-superiority language overlooks the sparse LPIPS reversal.

D1.justification: Appendix H documents duplicated RGB targets, the multi-output solve, mesh/color extraction, texture-atlas construction, ten named GSO assets and their access location. v2 also discloses SRB inputs of up to 100,000 points, while dropping the explicit KeOps implementation reference. Existing reconstruction settings and the project-code link remain available.

E1.justification: v2 extends coverage beyond geometry reconstruction to texture reconstruction, with quantitative evaluation on ten GSO objects and qualitative examples from Objaverse. Appendix A also adds a scene containing two identical chairs at different positions. Existing ShapeNet and SRB coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The SRB accuracy comparisons add SAP, DiGS, VisCo and OG-INR in v2 Tables 1 and 6. FFN and SIREN remain accuracy comparators but disappear from the SRB runtime comparison when it becomes Table 2. The ShapeNet comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The added texture experiment introduces a distinct evaluation protocol: 10,000 versus 2,500 sampled points, PSNR and LPIPS, and texture-atlas evaluation on the original mesh and UV coordinates to control for differences in reconstructed geometry. Appendix H specifies ten GSO objects. The retained geometry experiments preserve their splits, sampling settings, metrics and solvers.

E4.justification: New Appendix A and Figure 8 test positional consistency using two identical chairs within one scene, contrasting arc-cosine and Matérn reconstructions. The existing bandwidth, noise, category-generalization and convergence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bands. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds SRB scores for four comparators and new texture and positional-consistency results; retained geometry accuracy values are unchanged. New Table 3 reports Matérn versus arc-cosine PSNR of 19.61 versus 19.34 at 10,000 points and 18.92 versus 18.88 at 2,500 points. Sparse LPIPS instead favors arc-cosine, 2.09 versus 2.15. The FFN and SIREN runtimes of 337.91 and 599.00 seconds in v1 are removed.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix H add a limited extension from scalar signed-distance prediction to four outputs: signed distance and RGB. It concatenates color targets into the existing KRR solve and interpolates colors onto extracted surfaces. The underlying kernels, geometric reconstruction procedure and learned NKF framework remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 merges the former background and theoretical-analysis sections into Section 3, adds contribution bullets, rewrites selected explanations and the conclusion, and reorganizes the appendices. These are localized structural and language refinements within the retained overall narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds texture and positional-consistency figures and a texture-results table, expands SRB comparison tables, and separates runtime reporting. Several qualitative figures reorder method columns and add input-point or ground-truth panels. The existing RKHS-norm inset becomes numbered Figure 5. These changes substantially revise the visual presentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the four new SRB comparators, GSO, Objaverse and texture-atlas evaluation, while removing Charlier et al. (2021) and Peng et al. (2020). The core related-work narrative remains. Section 3.3 broadens the novelty statement from a Matérn/neural-network correspondence to a connection between SIRENs and kernel methods generally.

T1.justification: The reconstruction-error bound, optimal-bandwidth derivation and principal proofs already appear in v1 and are retained. v2 adds a centered arc-cosine definition and translation-invariance argument in Appendix A, plus Remark 7 extending the SIREN correspondence to stationary kernels generally. It omits the general half-integer Matérn expansion and explicit taper-kernel formula.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and assessability through the compact-support correction, input/ground-truth panels, broader SRB comparisons and an explicitly geometry-controlled texture protocol. The gains are limited: the main geometry results and proofs are retained, texture evaluation covers only ten GSO objects, and the superiority claim overlooks worse sparse LPIPS in Table 3. Removing FFN/SIREN timing evidence also narrows the runtime comparison.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Matérn-kernel reconstruction work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reorganization and added material.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds texture-reconstruction results on GSO and Objaverse and a positional-consistency demonstration.

before.justification: v1 reports original ShapeNet and SRB reconstruction experiments, learned-kernel comparisons, noise tests, generalization results and convergence analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

title: Matérn Kernels for Tunable Implicit Surface Reconstruction

C1.justification: The introduction qualifies the NTK equivalences with fixed bottom-layer weights and, for SIRENs, particular initializations. It also replaces the affine-equivalence claim with scaling plus another kernel. The broad reconstruction and performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds an interpretation of the revised Laplace/arc-cosine relationship through a valid residual kernel and distinguishes the NTK with all parameters trained. Empirical interpretations and existing noise-related qualifications are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times and code/data access information are retained. The ShapeNet, SRB and texture details shift across appendix pages without new technical disclosures.

E1.justification: Both versions use ShapeNet, SRB, GSO and Objaverse with the same reconstruction, texture, out-of-category generalization and noisy-input scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in each matched experiment, including NS/NS* and the kernel-free methods on SRB, arc-cosine for texture, and NKF* and NKSR in the robustness comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices F–H retain the same splits, sample counts, bandwidth sweeps, noise levels, metrics, solvers and timing procedures. Settings appearing on different appendix pages were already documented in v2.

E4.justification: The bandwidth-sensitivity analysis, stationarity examples in Appendix A, noise tests in Table 5, convergence comparison and supplementary qualitative examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version introduces repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates for the reported comparisons.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6, plotted results and qualitative reconstructions retain the same outcomes. For example, Table 4 reports Matérn 1/2 versus NKSR IoU values of 95.3 versus 95.6 in both versions.

M1.justification: The Matérn reconstruction procedure, Nyström/FALKON variant, texture extension and NKF-based learned kernels are unchanged. The revised neural-network discussion concerns their theoretical characterization.

P1.justification: Rewriting is localized to introductory qualifications, Corollary 5 and its proof, with an additional explanatory paragraph. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures and tables retain their content and display structure. The expanded proof changes equation layout and reflows subsequent appendix text; for example, Section H.1 begins on page 21 instead of page 19.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work section are unchanged, but the relationship to prior arc-cosine/ReLU-NTK results is qualified. Appendix E now invokes the already cited Chen and Xu (2021) for the full NTK decomposition instead of directly identifying it with the first-order arc-cosine kernel.

T1.justification: Corollary 5 and Appendix E substantially revise the claimed theoretical relationship. v2 asserts RKHS equality between Laplace and first-order arc-cosine kernels and an affine relationship. v3 instead identifies the RKHS with a sum involving zeroth- and first-order arc-cosine terms, explicitly decomposes the fully trained ReLU NTK, and derives scaling plus a positive-definite residual kernel in Equations (14)–(16). Theorem 3 and its existing initialization assumptions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves theoretical precision by distinguishing fixed-layer and fully trained NTKs and replacing v2's direct equivalence claim with an explicit decomposition and residual-kernel derivation in Corollary 5 and Appendix E. The introductory qualifications also better reflect the existing theorem assumptions. This is a focused improvement to the argument; the reconstruction method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.

A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–I. Content can be reliably matched across the appendix page shifts.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and their quantitative and qualitative outcomes, including Tables 1–6 and the appendix reconstructions.

before.justification: v2 reports original surface and texture reconstruction experiments, runtime measurements, generalization tests and noise-robustness results in Section 4 and the appendices.

title: Matérn Kernels for Tunable Implicit Surface Reconstruction

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and concluding claim retain the same central assertions: define n-RASP-L, train looped Transformers using final-answer and step-count supervision, and improve length generalization through adaptive depth.

C2.justification: v1 describes confidence stopping as selecting near-perfect accuracy without distinguishing aggregation. v3 explains that per-sample stopping works substantially worse on non-converging Parity and Binary Sum, connecting reliability to convergence. Section 7 also newly states that the current n-RASP-L definition excludes tasks requiring multiple sequential loops. These materially qualify applicability.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents EMA with factor 0.9999 for Parity/Binary Sum and specifies the fixed-depth FOP comparator's depth. Table 2 provides task-specific head counts and revised hyperparameters. Conversely, v1's disclosure of 4–6 hours per run on an NVIDIA A100 40 GB is removed. Code access and most implementation information remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Parity, repeated-token Copy, Binary Addition, Binary Sum, Binary Multiplication, and Unique Set with the same task requirements. Revised length ranges and stopping procedures remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 7 adds FOP-Loop-Fixed, a fixed-depth full-output comparator distinct from the retained NTP-Loop baseline. Other NTP and FAP/FOP comparators remain. UT and PonderNet appear in a descriptive architectural table, not a new empirical benchmark.

E3.justification: Reported configurations change materially: Parity uses 64 rather than 8 heads; Binary Sum uses 16 rather than 8 heads and 2 rather than 3 block layers. Both curriculum intervals change from 1000 to 500 updates. Parity's stated training interval changes from [1,20) to [1,20], while plotted test maxima contract from 50 to 40 for Parity and 30 to 24 for Binary Sum. v3 also adds per-sample versus whole-test-set stopping and a fixed-depth control. Updated curves therefore cannot be treated as same-setting performance changes.

E4.justification: v3 Appendix C adds a six-task comparison testing the effects of oracle, whole-test-set confidence, per-sample confidence, and fixed-depth stopping. Existing input-injection and pause-token ablations remain, with revised Parity/Binary Sum panels. Most additional stepwise traces from v1 Appendix C disappear; its 40-digit Parity trace moves into the main text.

E5.justification: Both experimental-details appendices report mean exact-match accuracy and standard errors from five training runs with different random seeds. v3 retains this practice rather than introducing additional runs or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Parity and Binary Sum curves are replaced under revised settings, and v1's report of Parity accuracy above 0.95 at 100 digits is removed. New Figure 7 shows approximately chance-level per-sample stopping on Parity and very low accuracy on Binary Sum despite strong oracle/batch results. The measured inference-time table, including 0.1967 seconds for oracle stopping and 0.2190 seconds for confidence stopping, is also removed.

M1.justification: The recurrent decoder-only architecture, input injection, NoPE, final-output loss, and step-supervised training are retained. FAP becomes FOP. The corrected argmin agrees with v1's minimum-loss description, while batch notation clarifies stopping aggregation; these do not establish a changed underlying algorithm.

P1.justification: Full-answer prediction/FAP becomes full-output prediction/FOP throughout. There are localized prose revisions, expanded stopping and related-work explanations, reorganized appendices, and subdivided experimental details. The main narrative and section order remain, alongside ICLR headers, author-year citations, and new acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v3 adds an architectural comparison table and a six-panel stopping comparison, removes the timing table and most supplementary stopping traces, and relocates the main ablation figure to Appendix B. The hyperparameter table gains a head-count column, and Parity/Binary Sum plot axes and captions change. These substantially revise the evidence displays beyond template changes and renumbering.

R1.justification: Section 5 expands the Universal Transformer/PonderNet comparison into Table 1, emphasizes claimed FOP and step-supervision innovations, and adds Bolukbasi et al. (2017). The remaining research positioning and cited works are largely retained.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 explicitly adds preprocessing/postprocessing stages and requires these and the repeated step to belong to RASP-L; v1 already used such stages in its examples and footnote. Equation 2 corrects argmax to argmin of cross-entropy. The three propositions, appendix programs, and asymptotic complexity analysis otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 makes adaptive-inference evidence more informative by adding a fixed-depth control, exposing per-sample stopping failures, clarifying aggregation, and correcting the loss-minimization equation. Explicit applicability limits also improve interpretation. These gains modestly outweigh the narrower reported length tests and removal of useful runtime and hardware information.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Looped Transformers for Length Generalization, with matching authors, framework, tasks, and appendix programs. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and reports additional comparisons of oracle, whole-test-set, per-sample, and fixed-depth stopping in Appendix C.

before.justification: v1 reports original six-task length-generalization experiments, ablations, stopping analyses, and measured inference times in Section 6 and the appendices.

title: Looped Transformers for Length Generalization

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: defining n-RASP-L tasks and improving length generalization through step-dependent supervision and adaptive looping without intermediate-output supervision.

C2.justification: Interpretations of input injection, convergence, and batch versus per-sample stopping are retained. Section 7 preserves the limitations concerning multiple successive loops, computational cost, limited training lengths, positional embeddings, and required training-step counts.

D1.justification: Appendix A, Listing 4 adds seq_map and firsts definitions, repairs malformed select code, and adds a reduction argument to kqv. However, kqv passes that argument to aggr_mean, whose displayed definition does not accept it. Experimental implementation settings and the code-access URL remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Parity, Copy with repeated binary tokens, Binary Addition, Binary Sum, restricted Binary Multiplication, and Unique Set. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.
